acceptanceCriteria.statement: Exactly one primary call-to-action element is present and reachable via keyboard on both the home and pricing screens, with no competing secondary action of equal visual weight.
At the mobile breakpoint, the home hero collapses to a single vertical column and the primary CTA is reachable without any horizontal scroll.
At the mobile breakpoint, pricing tiers stack vertically in their original relative order, with tier hierarchy (e.g., featured vs. standard) visually preserved.
Navigation item order on the migrated home and pricing screens matches the generic structural order observed in the inspected snapshot.
Every interactive element on both screens exhibits a visible, non-regressed keyboard focus indicator distinct from its resting and hover states.
The pricing screen contains only tiers, features, and CTAs grounded in the inspected snapshot; no additional tiers, customer counts, or partner logos are introduced.
No proprietary wordmark, exact palette value, unique illustration, or verbatim copy from the source site appears anywhere in the migrated surface.

accessibilityAndRecovery: Keyboard focus must remain visible on all nav links, the primary CTA, and pricing card interactive elements, matching the focus visibility already present on the inspected pages per the brief's non-regression constraint.
Heading structure on both screens uses a single top-level heading per screen with nested subheadings, supporting screen-reader navigation between hero and pricing sections.
Tier price and name information is exposed as real text content, not solely conveyed through color or size, so assistive technology users can perceive pricing hierarchy.
If responsive stacking triggers at an unexpected width, focus order continues to follow the visual top-to-bottom order rather than jumping between columns.
assumptions: The exact copy, wordmark, and palette of the source home and pricing pages are not reproduced here; only structural and generic stylistic principles are adapted per the brief's originality constraint.
The number and names of pricing tiers are assumed to match whatever was captured in the inspected snapshot; this candidate does not invent tier counts beyond what the brief implies was present.

Specific breakpoint pixel values for the mobile stacking rules are not specified in the brief and are left as an implementation detail bounded by the requirement of single-column stacking without horizontal scroll.
The account route referenced in the source site is out of scope and no claim in this candidate relies on it.

principles: Preserve a single primary call to action reachable from both the home and pricing routes, never introducing a competing secondary CTA in the hero or nav.
Keep navigation item order and hero hierarchy exactly as structurally observed on the inspected home page, expressed only as generic layout, not literal copy.
Collapse hero and pricing layouts to a single vertical column at the mobile breakpoint, preserving reading order and tier hierarchy without horizontal scroll.
Differentiate pricing tiers through typographic weight and card structure rather than through invented tier counts, prices, or partner logos not present in the snapshot.
Maintain visible keyboard focus states on every interactive element across both screens, matching or exceeding the focus visibility already observed on the inspected pages.
globalDirection.summary: An original B2B marketing surface covering home and pricing, retaining the inspected structural skeleton (nav order, hero hierarchy, mobile stacking, single primary CTA) while adapting card and hierarchy treatments observed in the corpus to avoid reproducing the source's proprietary copy, wordmark, palette, or illustrations.

accessibility: Primary CTA has a visible focus outline distinct from hover state.
Heading hierarchy uses a single h1 for the hero headline followed by logically nested subheadings.
Nav links are reachable in source order via sequential tab traversal.
failureAndRecovery: If hero imagery fails to load, headline and CTA remain legible against a fallback solid background so the value proposition is not lost.
If viewport width falls between breakpoints, stacking triggers early rather than allowing partial two-column overlap that would clip the CTA.
mobileRules: hero columns collapse to a single vertical stack at the mobile breakpoint
primary call to action remains reachable without horizontal scroll
screenBlueprints.summary: Hero-led landing screen stacking a headline, supporting value proposition line, and one primary CTA above the fold, with nav order retained from the inspected snapshot.

accessibility: Each pricing card exposes its tier name and price as programmatically associated text, not purely as styled visual weight.
Focus order moves top-to-bottom through stacked tiers on mobile matching the visual stacking order.
The single primary CTA within the pricing screen retains the same focus-visible treatment as the home screen CTA.
failureAndRecovery: If a tier's feature list is empty or not yet populated, the card retains its border and price header so the layout does not collapse or misalign adjacent cards.
If viewport width shrinks mid-session, tier stacking order is preserved so a user mid-comparison does not lose their place.
mobileRules: pricing tiers stack vertically and preserve their tier hierarchy at the mobile breakpoint
screenBlueprints.summary: Pricing comparison screen presenting tiers as bordered, low-elevation cards with price-forward hierarchy, stacking vertically on mobile while preserving relative tier order.

sourceDecisions.rationale: Brief mandates navigation item order, hero hierarchy, and mobile stacking behavior observed on the inspected pages be retained as generic structural principles.

Brief requires a single primary call to action reachable from either inspected page; the leatherback-co evidence demonstrates how a single-CTA pattern reduces decision paralysis, supporting retention of this constraint as a structural rule rather than a stylistic add-on.
Adapt the pill-cornered, low-elevation, hairline-border card treatment so pricing rows carry the visual load instead of the container, letting first-time visitors compare tiers at the data level.

Adapt the saturated-header / muted-body card split so the eye locks onto the price and tier name before descending into feature justification, matching the brief's job of comparing pricing tiers quickly.

Adapt the practice of reserving one accent color for the single primary action or metric, so the migrated surface's one primary CTA remains the unmistakable focal point without inventing a proprietary palette.
Reject icon-only navigation in favor of labeled nav items, since the migrated surface serves mixed-audience marketing visitors on their first visit, where clarity outweighs chrome density.
Reject the dual-CTA best practice (primary plus secondary 'learn more') because the brief mandates exactly one primary call to action per screen, avoiding dilution of the conversion path.
Reject neumorphic soft-shadow elevation for pricing cards because it reduces price-column contrast on bright screens, spending a contrast budget better allocated to the comparison data itself.
Reject reuse of any source-observed exact palette or unique illustration per the brief's originality constraint; only generic material or texture principles may be adapted, not literal color values.
